nodes.name: Monthly on the 1st
nodes.notes: 07:00 NZ on the first of the month, after the previous month has closed.

nodes.name: Run on demand
nodes.notes: Lets the workflow be triggered outside the schedule — for a re-run after a data correction, and for `n8n execute --id`, which is how the committed run in VERIFICATION.md was produced.

nodes.name: Get fact pack
nodes.notes: The engine container. n8n ships no Python interpreter and cannot see the repo on the host, so the two services talk over HTTP. Every number in the briefing originates behind this endpoint.

nodes.name: Get prompt and schema
nodes.notes: Fetched, not pasted into a node parameter. The prompt lives in prompts/v2_final.md and is served by the engine, so the workflow and the CLI cannot drift onto different instructions.

nodes.name: Build model request
nodes.notes: Mirrors src/providers.py. The schema comes from the engine, so the constraint the model is held to is the same one the tests assert against.

nodes.name: Write the briefing
nodes.notes: The key comes from the container environment, never from this file. responseSchema constrains the response server-side, so the model cannot return a briefing that is missing a section — the same guarantee the CLI gets.

nodes.name: Assemble briefing
nodes.notes: Prose from the model, every table and every figure from the fact pack — the same split src/render.py enforces.

nodes.name: Save to disk
nodes.notes: Mounted to ./output on the host. This is the delivery demonstrated in the screenshot.

nodes.name: Post to Slack
nodes.notes: DISABLED ON PURPOSE. No Slack workspace was available, so this node is wired and left off rather than faked. Set SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL and enable it; nothing else changes.
